purpose: Phase 9 chapter rebuild active sequence. Prototype levels 01-15 remain as reference scenes but are no longer the active progression.

chapters.title: First Rescue
chapters.purpose: Teach automatic movement, exits, pit preview, and wall-turn behavior before abilities appear.

chapters.title: Holding the Crowd
chapters.purpose: Teach Blocker as the first player-controlled direction and crowd-control ability.

levels.title: Walk Home
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce automatic walking and the exit in a calm first level.
map_logic: One continuous floor leads directly to the exit.
No pit, wall, or ability is present.
The level confirms spawning, automatic walking, and rescue counting.
intended_solution: Do nothing.
All movers walk into the exit.
failure_logic: Failure should only happen if the time limit is too short or the exit is misplaced.

levels.title: Mind the Edge
levels.teaching_goal: Preview pits as visible danger without requiring an ability yet.
map_logic: The exit is placed before a clearly marked red pit.
The pit is visible as a future warning but should not be reached in normal play.
The player learns that red gaps are dangerous.
intended_solution: Do nothing.
All movers enter the exit before the pit.
failure_logic: If the exit route is missed in layout testing, movers continue into the visible pit.

levels.title: The Long Floor
levels.teaching_goal: Increase walking distance and spawned mover count while staying ability-free.
map_logic: A longer floor gives the player time to observe the queue.
Four movers spawn with a slower rhythm.
No ability or terrain hazard is required.
intended_solution: Do nothing.
Watch all four movers reach the far exit.
failure_logic: The only intended failure is a time-limit tuning issue.

levels.title: First Turn
levels.teaching_goal: Teach that movers turn around when they hit a wall.
map_logic: Movers spawn near the middle and initially walk right.
A red wall on the right turns them back left.
The exit is on the left side of the same floor.
intended_solution: Do nothing.
Movers hit the wall, turn left, and enter the exit.
failure_logic: Bad wall or exit placement can trap movers or make the route too slow.

levels.title: Stand Here
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce Blocker as a deliberate sacrifice that turns the crowd away from danger.
map_logic: Movers spawn on a single floor and initially walk right toward a marked pit.
The exit is safely placed on the left side of the same floor.
One blocker must stand between the spawn and the right-side pit.
intended_solution: Select Blocker.
Turn the first mover into a blocker before it reaches the pit.
The remaining movers turn left and enter the exit.
failure_logic: No blocker means the group walks into the right pit.
Blocking too late loses the rescue target.

levels.title: Late Turn
levels.teaching_goal: Make the blocker point later and more deliberate while keeping timing readable.
map_logic: A longer floor gives more time to read the route.
The right pit remains the visible failure point.
The left exit rewards using the blocker as a turn marker.
intended_solution: Wait until the lead mover approaches the right danger zone.
Apply Blocker before the pit.
Rescue the following three movers at the left exit.
failure_logic: Blocking too early may slow the route and make the lesson weaker.
Blocking too late sends too many movers into the pit.

levels.title: Lower Shelf
levels.teaching_goal: Teach using Blocker after a drop onto a lower platform.
map_logic: Movers start on an upper shelf and fall to a lower shelf.
The lower exit is left of the landing area.
The right side of the lower shelf leads to a marked pit.
intended_solution: Let the lead mover fall to the lower platform.
Apply Blocker on the lower platform before the right pit.
The remaining movers turn left into the exit.
failure_logic: Blocking on the upper shelf stops the intended route.
Blocking after the lower danger point loses too many movers.

levels.title: Two-Way Lesson
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce two available blockers on one floor with danger visible on both sides.
map_logic: A wide floor has marked danger beyond both ends.
The exit is left of the spawn area.
Two blockers are available so the player can experiment with controlling the group.
intended_solution: Use a blocker to prevent the group from walking into the first danger direction.
Use the second blocker only if needed to stabilize the group near the exit path.
Rescue three movers.
failure_logic: Spending both blockers away from the route can prevent enough movers from reaching the exit.
Ignoring either edge eventually sends movers into danger.

levels.title: Crowd Control
levels.teaching_goal: Summarize Chapter 2 with a wider one-blocker sacrifice puzzle.
map_logic: Five movers spawn on a wide floor and face a right-side pit.
The exit is on the left side.
The chapter ends by asking for one clean blocker placement and four rescues.
intended_solution: Use the first mover as a blocker before the right pit.
Let the other four movers turn left and enter the exit.
failure_logic: No blocker means the crowd walks into danger.
A late blocker can make the rescue target impossible.
